title: docs(spec): `FlowSchema.successMessage` / `errorMessage` still describe themselves as screen-flow-only, after #9414 makes every terminal run carry them
body:
Blocked-by: #9414

Found while implementing #9414. Filed rather than fixed there: it lands in
`packages/spec` (and the two generated reference pages that mirror the `describe()` text),
which is a different package and a different gate family from the engine repair, and it
only becomes wrong once #9414's PR merges.

## Measured

`packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts`, `origin/main` @ `e3a86e390`:

```ts
/**
 * Terminal messages for `screen`-flow runs. When the run reaches a terminal
 * state, the UI flow-runner shows `successMessage` instead of a generic
 * "Done" toast, and `errorMessage` instead of the raw error. …
 */
successMessage: z.string().optional().describe('Toast shown when a screen flow completes (defaults to a generic "Done").'),
errorMessage: z.string().optional().describe('Toast shown when a screen flow fails (defaults to the raw error).'),
```

The sibling declaration on `AutomationResult`
(`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`) has always been general — "set on
terminal success … on failure" — and #9414 makes the engine match it: `execute()`,
`executeWithoutRetry()` and `retryExecution()`'s exhausted exit all carry the pair, so a
flow dispatched through `POST /api/v1/automation/:name/trigger` gets the author's text
whether or not it is a screen flow.

After that lands, the authoring surface is the only place still saying "screen flow", and
it is the place an author reads first.

## Why it is worth a card rather than a comment

This wording is the exact premise of the alternative route that was **considered and
rejected** at #9414's triage — "narrow the contract text to say these are screen-flow /
resume-only" — which was rejected because it deletes a declared, documented,
console-consumed capability to make a bug disappear. Leaving the authoring surface phrased
that way keeps that reading alive and reachable for the next reader.

## Scope

Two `describe()` strings and the JSDoc above them. The text is mirrored into
`content/docs/references/automation/flow.mdx` and
`content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx`, so those move with it. Nothing about the
schema's shape, validation or generated `authorable-surface.base.json` changes — the
descriptions are not part of that artifact (checked).
